87.6E, APPROXIMATELY 517 NM EAST-SOUTHEAST OF CHENNAI, INDIA. ANIMATED 
ENHANCED INFRARED IMAGERY (EIR) DEPICTS DISORGANIZED CONVECTION 
PARTIALLY OBSCURING A LOOSELY DEFINED LOW-LEVEL CIRCULATION. A 121549Z 
ASCAT PASS REVEALS A BROAD AREA OF LIGHT WINDS AND 20 KT WESTERLIES 
ALONG THE SOUTHERN PERIPHERY. ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS INDICATES A 
FAVORABLE AREA FOR DEVELOPMENT WITH LOW TO MODERATE VERTICAL WIND SHEAR 
(15-20KTS), RADIAL OUTFLOW, AND VERY WARM SEA SURFACE TEMPERATURES (29-
30C). GLOBAL DETERMINISTIC AND ENSEMBLE MODELS DEPICT GRADUAL 
DEVELOPMENT OVER THE NEXT 48 HOURS AS THE SYSTEM TRANSITS NORTHWESTWARD. 
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED SURFACE WINDS ARE ESTIMATED AT 13 TO 18 KNOTS. MINIMUM 
SEA LEVEL PRESSURE IS ESTIMATED TO BE NEAR 1009 MB. THE POTENTIAL FOR 
THE DEVELOPMENT OF A SIGNIFICANT TROPICAL CYCLONE WITHIN THE NEXT 24 
HOURS IS LOW.
